text:
anya: quick follow-up on the kernel-autotune thread — we've been seeing prefill jitter on low-seq, small-batch workloads that churns the KV cache and causes repeated probe sweeps. thinking about two lightweight mitigations to test. :thinking:

samir: can you paste a log snippet showing the churn?

anya: sure, pasted a short example from prod-canary last night:
```
[2026-03-18 02:14:12] probe: kernels tried=[k_fast32,k_generic,k_quant] probes=3; cache_evictions=7; prefill=true; seq_len=32; batch_size=2
[2026-03-18 02:14:13] probe: kernels tried=[k_fast32,k_generic] probes=2; cache_evictions=5; prefill=false; seq_len=28; batch_size=1
```

anya: proposal sketch: 1) sampling-based cold kernel selection (sample a single promising kernel using a tiny micro-benchmark instead of sweeping every candidate), 2) ephemeral affinity buckets for prefill + soft-TTL eviction to reduce thrash, and 3) adaptive probe budget tied to seq-len variance.

lucas: how would ephemeral affinity differ from our current bucketed-cache? sounds similar to shape-bucketing but with time dimension?

anya: right — affinity buckets are short-lived tags (affinity_id) that group kernels/kv cache entries for recent sequences. each bucket has soft-ttl (e.g. 8-30s) and a score that decays. eviction prefers low-score buckets rather than LRU across all sequences, so small hot-traffic patterns keep KV entries longer while noisy sporadic sequences don't push everything out.

ciara: can you show the pseudo-config?

anya: here's a rough config I used in the simulation:
```yaml
ephemeral_affinity:
  ttl_seconds: 12
  affinity_window_s: 300   # max grouping window for similar seq shapes
  decay_alpha: 0.75       # exponential decay for bucket score
  probe_penalty: 2.0      # score penalty per probe triggered
  min_reserve_per_bucket: 4
```

samir: i like the idea. for sampling-based selection do you mean run a short (2-4 token) microbenchmark at probe time to estimate throughput for the candidate kernel? that's cheaper than full probe but still extra work.

anya: exactly. microbenchmark would use a synthetic sequence (e.g., 8 tokens) and measure per-token ms on the current hardware path. we only do it for the coldest affinity candidates and cache the micro-results for the bucket duration.

lucas: concern: prefill currently forces probe during prefill path which could amplify jitter if microbenchmarks add latency to the initial user request. maybe schedule microbench asynchronously and use a fallback kernel synchronously?

ciara: +1 to async probe. fallback chosen by a lightweight heuristic: if seq_len < 64 and batch_size <=2 prefer low-latency kernel; else use sampled result when available. also suggests an "emergency probe budget" cap per-worker to avoid storming hardware.

autotune-bot: NOTE: if we run canary, default canary config: traffic 10%, duration 48h, metrics to capture = [p50 latency, p95 latency, probe_count_per_request, cache_hit_rate, thrash_index].

samir: what's thrash_index?

anya: simple metric proposal: thrash_index = eviction_count / max(1, unique_affinity_buckets). gives signal when one pattern is evicting many others.

lucas: also add probe_cost_ms = sum(probe_durations) per-second to the dashboard. if probe_cost_ms rises > baseline*1.5 revert automatically.

ciara: i'll wire up the dashboard tiles and set alert: p95 latency increase > 10% or probe_cost_ms > 1.5x baseline. will also track cache_hit_rate by affinity.

anya: plan: i'll draft a short RFC with experiments: (A) sampling-only (async) + affinity soft-ttl, (B) sampling + adaptive probe budget (stddev of seq_len window), (C) noop control. run each on 10% canary slices for 48h and compare thrash_index + p95. looking for reduced probes and higher stable cache_hit_rate.

samir: volunteers for running microbench harness? i can help implement the lightweight timer and integrate into the probe path.

lucas: i'll add guardrail code to force fallback and automatic rollback if p95 regresses.

ciara: i'll own dashboarding and the alert rules. ping me when you open the RFC doc.

anya: thanks all. i'll post the RFC link once it's up. tagging @ciara for alerts, @samir for harness, @lucas for guardrails. :thumbsup:
